**Example**

**Question:** Determine the voltage at the points A, B, C and D of the circuit in figure 11.09 (a).

**Solutions:** Voltage at C and D is 0, voltage at A is $3\text{ V}$. To calculate the voltage at B, current $I$ of the circuit has to be determined.

$$I = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{3}{1 + 2} \text{ A} = 1.0 \text{ A}$$

So, the reduction in voltage from A to B is,

$$V = RI = 1 \, \Omega \times 1 \text{ A} = 1 \text{ V}$$

So, voltage at point B, $3 \text{ V} - 1 \text{ V} = 2 \text{ V}$

As the voltage (potential) at all points has been found, verify whether Ohm's law works or not?

**Question:** Determine the voltages at the points A, B, C, D and E of the circuit in figure 11.9 (b).

**Solution:** Voltage at D is zero

Voltage at A is $6\text{ V}$
